[90m│[0m                                                                              [90m│[0m
[90m│[0m  Five stages, each a few short lessons and one task to pass:                 [90m│[0m
[90m│[0m                                                                              [90m│[0m
[90m│[0m  Everything you type runs in a real shell. The tutor made a practice         [90m│[0m
[90m│[0m  folder for you and only ever writes there. No timer, no score; try as       [90m│[0m

[1;97mOrientation[0m

Below this panel is a real shell prompt. It looks like:

[90mshelltutor>[0m

Type a command there and press Enter; the shell runs it. Four words
steer the tutor instead: [92mnext[0m, [92mprev[0m, [92mshow[0m and [92mquit[0m. A fifth, [92mcheck[0m,
appears when a stage's task is ready to be tested.

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m to begin Stage 1.[0m

[1;97mStage 1: Where am I?[0m

Five short lessons, then a task. You'll run your first commands and

learn the few keys that make a shell comfortable.

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m for lesson 1.1.[0m

[1;97mRunning a command[0m

A command is a name, then the words you hand it. [1mecho[0m is the simplest

one: it repeats its words back to you.

  [92mecho hello[0m                   [90m# prints hello, then the prompt returns[0m
  [92mecho I am at the shell[0m       [90m# spaces separate the words[0m
  [92mecho "I am at the shell"[0m     [90m# quotes make them one word[0m

Notice the quotes never print. They only group.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m
echo I am at the shell
echo I am at the shell

[1;97mFour keys[0m

These keys make the shell comfortable. Try each one now.

[1mTab[0m       finishes a word: type [92mecho p[0m, press Tab, then Enter
  [1m↑[0m         brings back your last line; Enter runs it again
  [1mCtrl+C[0m    throws away the line you are typing; a fresh prompt
  [1mCtrl+L[0m    clears the screen; type [92mshow[0m to bring this lesson back

[1mCtrl+C[0m is the way out at a prompt. Inside a full-screen program
(you'll meet one in Stage 3) the way out is [1mq[0m.

[93m▶ Try each key, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWhere am I, who am I, when is it[0m

The tutor made a folder for you to practise in. Ask the system where

it is, who you are, and what time it is.

  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# where: the folder you are in[0m
  [92mwhoami[0m     [90m# who: your user name[0m
  [92mdate[0m       [90m# when: the date and time[0m

[92mpwd[0m printed the full name of your practice folder.
This prompt ends in [92m>[0m. An ordinary bash prompt usually ends in [92m$[0m.

[93m▶ Run all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mThe shell, caught in the act[0m

Type a real command, then the same letters scrambled.

[92mdate[0m     [90m# prints the date and time[0m
  [92mdtae[0m     [90m# bash: dtae: command not found[0m

[1mbash:[0m is the shell speaking. It looked for a program named dtae and
found none. A stray / in front or a missing space earns the same kind
of message: read it, then type the line again.

[1mterminal[0m → [1mshell[0m → [1mprogram[0m: the window, bash, and date.

[93m▶ Try both, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWho else types here[0m

Every command goes terminal → shell → program. An AI assistant that

"runs commands" for you goes the same way: it types a line, the shell
finds the program, the program runs.

So three habits count twice, for you and for a helper:
  read the line before anyone presses Enter
  know which folder it will run in
  read what comes back

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m for Stage 1's task.[0m

[1;97mSTAGE 1 — GATE[0m

[1mRecall[0m (three questions, all three must be correct).

First, three questions. Type your answer in words; this is not the shell.

Then a [1mpractical task[0m: run a few commands and tell me what
they printed. The script verifies your answers.

[90mUnlimited retries. No skip.[0m
[93m┃[0m 1 of 3   In a normal bash window (not this tutor), which character usually
[93m┃[0m 3 of 3   After [92mwhoami[0m runs, where does its output go?

[1;97mSTAGE 1 — GATE TASK[0m

Inside the practice prompt, run each of these once. Read each output.

Then type [92mcheck[0m.

  [92mwhoami[0m
  [92mpwd[0m
  [92mdate[0m

After all three have run, I'll ask you what each one printed.
[90mOnly commands you type after this screen count. This task runs in
/var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-b1vp37td/stage1; [92mpwd[90m shows it.[0m

[93m▶ Type [92mcheck[93m only after running all three.[0m
[1;90mcheck[0m [90m(test your work)[0m   [1;90mshow[0m [90m(the task again)[0m   [1;90mquit[0m [90m(save and leave)[0m
[1mThree short follow-ups based on what you saw.[0m

[93m┃[0m What did [92mpwd[0m print? (paste the full path)
[93m┃ ?[0m

[93m┃[0m What day of the week did [92mdate[0m show? Type just the day, for example Sat.
[93m┃ ?[0m

[1;97mStage 1 cleared[0m

You can now

  say something back           [92mecho[0m
  find where you are           [92mpwd[0m
  find out who you are, when   [92mwhoami   [0m [92mdate[0m

clear the screen             [92mclear    [0m [92mCtrl+L[0m
  finish a name, reuse a line  [92mTab      [0m [92mUp[0m
  stop a running command       [92mCtrl+C[0m

Next: Stage 2 · Paths

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m to go on, or [92mquit[93m to stop here. Your place is saved.[0m

[1;97mStage 2: Paths[0m

Six short lessons, then a task. The shell is always standing in one

folder. You'll learn to see where, look around, and move.

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m for lesson 2.1.[0m

[1;97mWhere you are[0m

You are always standing in one folder: the [1mcurrent directory[0m. Here

is your practice folder, drawn as a tree:
  /var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-b1vp37td  [93m◀ you are here[0m
  ├── poem.txt
  ├── numbers.txt
  ├── stage1/
  └── stage2/

  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# predict what it prints, then run it[0m
The line [92mpwd[0m prints is the full name of the "you are here" folder.

[93m▶ Run [92mpwd[93m, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWhat is here[0m

[92mls[0m lists the names in the folder you are standing in.

[92mls[0m            [90m# the names[0m
  [92mls -p[0m         [90m# the same, with / after each folder[0m
  [92mls -a[0m         [90m# also the hidden names, which start with a dot[0m
  [92mls /[0m          [90m# a folder you are not in: the top of everything[0m

Notice stage1/ in the second listing: the slash means a folder you
could step into.

[93m▶ Try all four, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

Applications	Volumes		etc		private		var
Library		bin		home		sbin
System		cores		opt		tmp
Users		dev		pkg		usr

[1;97mMoving[0m

[92mcd[0m changes the folder you are standing in. It prints nothing; [92mpwd[0m

shows that it worked.

  [92mcd ..[0m      [90m# up one level, to the folder that contains this one[0m
  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# see where you are now[0m
  [92mcd -[0m       [90m# back to where you just were[0m

[92mcd..[0m with no space is a different word, and bash cannot find it.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mHome and back[0m

Every user has a home folder. [1m~[0m is its short name.

[92mcd[0m                 [90m# with nothing after it: go home[0m
  [92mpwd[0m                [90m# home is outside your practice folder[0m
  [92mcd /var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-b1vp37td[0m  [90m# come back, using the folder's full name[0m

A full name works from anywhere. That is what makes it a full name.

[93m▶ Go home and come back, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mNames for places[0m

A [1mpath[0m names a place. Three short names:
  [1m.[0m     here, the current directory

[1m..[0m    one level up
  [1m~[0m     your home folder

A [1mrelative[0m path starts where you are: in ~/projects, the name notes
means ~/projects/notes. An [1mabsolute[0m path starts from /, the top:
/usr/bin is the same place wherever you stand.
  [92mls ..[0m      [90m# look one level up without moving[0m
  [92mls ~[0m       [90m# look at home without moving[0m

[93m▶ Try both, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m
